sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Describes the sister lect Kyak [bka]; p. 377 says Kyak, Moo and Leelau 'could, linguistically at least, be considered dialects of the same language, since their lexical similarity is above 90%'. Sec. 3.3 Tones p. 379: 'Kyak has three contrastive lexical tones, High, Low, and Falling' (sem 'pot' / sem 'monkey' / sem 'servant'), downstep, phonetic mid tones.

sources.note: Nothing. Moo [gwg] is one of ten tone-marked wordlist columns; sec. 3.3 Tone (pp. 43-44): 'High, mid, low, falling and rising tones were noted... we decline to reconstruct tone for items where tone is too inconsistent'. The words 'stress'/'accent' occur 0 times.
